releaseNotes: The emotional-design cluster is de-duplicated: 139,655 to 120,560 bytes across four files, 19,095 removed, with zero files created, moved, renamed or deleted and every heading preserved verbatim. ARCHITECTURE.md has named this cluster since the north star was written — four files restating the same citations, twelve near-identical card files — and the directory moves landed while the merge never did. Headings stay because six of them are cited by exact heading-path from other files; only bodies became pointers.

A live contradiction was found and resolved, and it was wider than it first looked. emotional-experience-design.md and emotional-design-system.md disagreed on the six-lens score bands in TWO places, not one: a feature scoring exactly 6 was sent to redesign by one file and to refinement by the other, and 7-8 got a vague needs-refinement in one versus a concrete proceed-with-named-blockers-tracked-as-failure-cards in the other. An agent's verdict depended on which file it happened to load. Founder call: the stricter reading is canonical — score at or above 9 is build-ready, 7-8 proceeds with named blockers, below 7 is redesign before build. emotional-experience-design.md now states the canonical bands and records what it used to say and why that was wrong.

What was NOT done, deliberately. The two failure-card taxonomies still coexist: emotional-design-system.md defines an emotional-card-* set of which five of six IDs are confirmed orphans appearing in exactly one file, while emotional-experience-design.md defines the experience-card-* set that EMOTIONAL_AUDIT.md actually consumes. Converging them means changing which IDs agents emit into generated business repos — user-facing behaviour of the same class as the score-band call, so it needs the same sign-off rather than being bundled into a dedup diff by momentum. The divergence is documented rather than silently carried.

The dedup was anchored on headings, never line numbers. The first edit shifted every subsequent line, so a plan expressed in line ranges would have cut the wrong content from the second file onward. Every pointer target was then resolved against the real headings in ethics-guardrail.md rather than trusted, and that check caught two imprecise pointers: section 5 is Guardrail Contract with Non-Negotiable Prohibitions as a subsection under it, not a section by that name, and one reference left section 1 unnamed. A pointer to a section that does not exist is worse than the duplication it replaces.

Gates ran between every step rather than once at the end, so a break would be attributable to one change instead of to 19KB of deletions at once. check-reference-size, check-emotional-design and audit-skill-links were clean at baseline and after each of the five steps. Every file now sits under half the 64KB per-file budget: design-system 31,767, measurement 31,977, design 26,386, and ethics-guardrail untouched at 30,430 — this pass only ever pointed at that file, never edited it, so its headroom stays free for whatever the remaining taxonomy decision needs.
